To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two barley root proteins, Gs1 (26 kilodalton) and Gs2 (26 kilodaltons), increase in response to salt, are similar to germin, and are not regulated by abscisie acid.
Gs1 and the Gs2-like protein increase during salt stress and that Gs1, Gs2, and the Gs1-like protein accumulate during abscisie acid treatment.

the 26 kilodaltons Gs1 and 6.3/6.5 isoelectric point polypeptides that are induced by salt stress in barley roots are similar to germin, that they are present in the roots and coleoptile of the seedlings but not in leaves, and that their synthesis is affected by abscicic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and distribution of Gs1, Gs2, and a 25.4 kilodalton, isolectric point 6 polypeptides in barley.
the identification of a new family of proteins that increase in barley roots during salt stress.
the isolation and identification of two germin-like polypeptides, Gs1 (26 kilodalton) and Gs2 (26 kilodaltons), that increase in barley roots during salt stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Gs1 and the Gs1-related 25.5 kD polypeptide are not regulated by abscisidic acid.
the Gs1 and the Gs2 polypeptides that are induced by salt stress are related to germin.
the Gs1 and GS2 polypeptides increase in roots in response to salt and abscisic stress, and that the Gs2 polypeptide increases in response to abscisic treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
germin-like polypeptides increase in barley roots during salt stress.
Gs1 and the Gs2-like protein are heat stable and accumulate in roots during salt stress and in the coleoptile during abscisie acid treatment.
Gs1 and the 25.5 kD, isoelectric 6.1 protein are similar in structure and function, but are differentially regulated in response to abscisic-acid and salt-stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gs1 and 25.5 kDa polypeptide are synthesized in response to abscisic stress and are immunologically related.
the Gs1 and GS2 polypeptides are not regulated in the same way.
Gs1 and GS2 accumulate in barley roots under salt stress.
